A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Taking the GP Out of the Loop and the same TuRBO-ENN research. Text extraction and visual inspection cover all 14 pages of v2 and 21 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations and appendices.

before.justification: V2 reports original scaling experiments and optimization results on five simulation or hyperparameter-optimization tasks, including repeated runs under natural and frozen noise.

after.justification: V3 retains original optimization results and adds surrogate-fitting benchmarks, hyperparameter sensitivity experiments and acquisition ablations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the precision-weighted ENN surrogate, subsampled fitting, incumbent selection, RAASP candidates, noisy UCB and fitting-free NDS acquisition. The revised scalarization and variable-neighbor analysis in Appendix C are theoretical constructions, not documented changes to the implemented method.

E1.justification: V3 adds a distinct regression and held-out predictive-quality evaluation track on Ackley, Sphere, Booth and Rosenbrock (Section 5.4 and Appendices A–B). These functions already appeared among v2's optimizer tests, but the regression task is new. The five principal optimization tasks and their natural/frozen-noise coverage remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figures 3, 6 and 7 add actual comparisons with SMAC, DNGO and GP-UCB, although several attempted settings time out. Appendix A adds turbo-one-nds and turbo-one-ucb controls. Appendix B also evaluates two sparse-GP configurations, including the capped-inducing-point SVGP_linear variant.

E3.justification: New protocols include synthetic regression with independent training/test sets, Gaussian noise, predictive-error/log-likelihood metrics, fitting-size sweeps to one million observations, and normalized-rank evaluations. Appendix A.1 uses 1,000 training and 1,000 test points; Figure 8 uses 100 test points. Table 1 revises natural-noise LunarLander N from 300 to 10,000, matching v2 Figure 3's existing axis; this does not establish that additional optimization runs occurred.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained turbo-zero ablation, Appendix A tests K/P sensitivity in surrogate prediction and optimization, and isolates acquisition choice by replacing Thompson sampling with NDS or UCB while retaining TuRBO's GP. Tables 2–5 and Figures 9–15 provide substantial new evidence about parameter sensitivity and component effects.

E5.justification: The optimization experiments retain 30 runs and mean ± two standard errors. The new fitting protocol explicitly reports 10 replications with ± one standard error in Figure 8, shared with Figures 16–17; the new sensitivity tables also report uncertainty. There is no stated increase in repetitions for retained experiments.

E6.justification: V3 adds predictive-quality, fitting-time, sensitivity and acquisition-ablation results throughout Tables 2–5 and Figures 8–17. Existing timings also change: frozen-noise LunarLander's ENN proposal time changes from 0.6 to 0.9 seconds and its tabulated speedup from 89 to 58; frozen-noise Hopper's CMA-ES time changes from 7.0 to 5.2 seconds. Natural-noise LunarLander timings are replaced alongside the revised N entry, preventing a straightforward same-setting comparison.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix A is substantially reworked into v3 Appendix C. V3 replaces the full-K-neighbor radius argument with a bound on distant-neighbor weights, adds approximation and spacing bounds, and formalizes improvement properties for a shifted scalarization. New Theorems 2–3 provide conditional noisy weighted-kNN bias–variance/rate results and fitted-parameter stability transfers. V2's final algorithmic-consistency theorem is not retained.

C1.justification: The principal claims remain linear-cost ENN/TuRBO-ENN, comparable optimization quality with one-to-two-order proposal-time reductions up to 50,000 observations, and PBO convergence. The abstract's added 'without sacrificing solution quality' wording repeats claims already present in v2's contributions and conclusion.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies timing comparisons by contrasting its single-core allocation with multicore/GPU resources in cited studies. Appendix C interprets neighbor radius as controlling bias and squared weights as controlling effective noise averaging, and frames its PBO result as surrogate-side conditions for an auxiliary acquisition. Section 6's practical limitations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: Anonymous package and repository placeholders become the named ennbo package and an identifiable source location. V3 newly discloses one CPU core per run and specific fitting configurations, including sparse-GP inducing-point counts. These disclosures do not establish a hardware change for retained experiments.

R1.justification: V3 adds Lindauer et al. (SMAC3), Regis and Shoemaker (2013), and Wang et al. (2019, million-point exact GPs), including a discussion of hardware differences in the latter comparison. Snoek's neural-network work and Hutter's random-forest work were already cited in v2; the overall positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The former seven-part PBO appendix is extensively rewritten and reorganized into a four-part surrogate-theory exposition, alongside separate ablation and fitting appendices. Section 5 is reorganized into Simulators, Noise Handling, Results and Pure Fitting Tasks, with rewritten results prose. Acknowledgements and an impact statement are also added, while much of the introduction and method exposition remains.

P2.justification: Table 1 is transposed and expanded with comparator rows and explicit timeout entries. Figures 3–7 are redrawn with revised legends, comparator curves and placement. New sensitivity tables and fitting/acquisition displays substantially expand the visual presentation; Figure 8 redisplays the Ackley portion of the Appendix B fitting results.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses important validation gaps in v2 through held-out surrogate-quality tests, GP-based acquisition controls and systematic K/P sensitivity analyses. It also improves the local-consistency reasoning, adds conditional noisy-estimation theory and identifies the implementation. These substantially strengthen the paper's evidential support. Remaining inconsistencies limit the gain: Section 3 still says neural-network/random-forest methods are excluded, and the main text retains a convergence claim broader than Appendix C establishes.
